leads.summary: Helium installer skips the browser flags that pin the password backend and integrate other Chromium-family browsers
leads.consequence: The new Install/Defaults/Helium path installs helium-browser-bin and reports success without creating ~/.config/helium-browser-flags.conf, while its AUR wrapper actually reads that file. Unlike the other Chromium-family installers, Helium therefore lacks Omarchy's --password-store=gnome-libsecret, Wayland flags, automatic extension loading, initial theme setup and running theme-policy refresh. Even copying the Chromium flags does not register Helium's native messaging hosts (H10/H11). The existing migration explicitly explains that an autodetected backend change can make stored cookies/passwords unreadable. Manual/23-browsers.md:21 still lists only Chromium/Chrome/Edge/Brave as having the Omarchy extensions. Subsequent webapp launches continue on Helium without these settings. Configure the Helium flags and theme refresh at install, preserving user overrides; test setup beyond package installation.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Finding 1; password-store pin detail verified by coordinator (config/chromium-flags.conf:3, migrations/1784508556.sh:1-13) and published

leads.summary: Opera is offered as an app-mode web-app browser despite a related PR reporting that it ignores --app=
leads.consequence: Selecting Opera writes opera.desktop, and every subsequent existing webapp shortcut calls opera --app=URL. Open PR #8299 describes an observed Opera process with that flag opening its start page/restored tabs instead of the requested URL, and changes it to a positional URL, which opens a tab rather than an app window. This is a lead, not independently verified because Opera's release is closed-source and no isolated Opera runtime was available. Check the packaged Opera version in an isolated headed run before calling this a verified break; if confirmed, do not advertise Opera as a working Chromium app-window selection without a compatible launch contract. #8299's implementation has a merge-file conflict at merges/8299/result:24-42.
leads.triage: Opera hypothesis, pre-existing launcher behaviour; dropped

leads.summary: Notification failure makes the preference command report failure after changing the preference
leads.consequence: mv commits the new value before omarchy-notification-send runs. With an unavailable D-Bus notification service, the notification helper exits nonzero, so the selector exits nonzero even though the preference has changed. A caller that retries or treats failure as rollback sees contradictory state; the next webapp launch already uses the new browser. Verified in an isolated fixture with the notification backend returning 29: command exited 29, saved helium.desktop, next launch used Helium. Make notification best-effort or explicitly report partial success.
leads.triage: notification failure after write: minor edge, not published

leads.summary: Keep Ecosia recognition if the related launcher PR merges
leads.consequence: Open PR #11164 adds org.ecosia.Browser* and ecosia* to the regular-browser webapp whitelist, with a test expecting the Ecosia binary for an Ecosia XDG default. This PR rewrites that case into two whitelists without either token. A direct three-way merge against the other PR's own merge-base has conflict markers at merges/11164/result:17-26, so a resolution that takes this PR's patterns drops #11164 and falls back to Chromium, switching browser profile. Under an isolated fixture with both desktop files/executables present, the current head launches Chromium rather than Ecosia. Retain both recognized IDs in automatic and explicit validation when reconciling #11164; rerun its test with the new selector command available.
leads.triage: Ecosia #11164 conflict: verified PR OPEN via gh; published as related-PR note

leads.summary: The changed Helium installer test permits skipping all post-package browser setup
leads.consequence: This test's real-installer Helium branch asserts only the package stub was called and the default ID was set. It passed at this head even though the Helium branch omits flags, extension setup and theme refresh, whereas the neighboring Chromium and Zen real-installer cases check their setup calls and output. A plausible mutant removing post-package setup remains green; add assertions for the Helium flags/config and setup when fixing H1.
leads.triage: test gap for Helium setup; subsumed by F1, not published separately

leads.summary: Reconcile wrapped desktop Exec launchers with the related full-Exec fixes
leads.consequence: The newly rewritten desktop lookup retains only the first space-delimited Exec token. A valid custom desktop entry `Exec=/usr/bin/env LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD chromium %U` therefore passes --app= to env instead of Chromium. Isolated head run exited 125 with '/usr/bin/env: unrecognized option --app=...' and never invoked the browser. This parser limitation existed in the old launcher but is being independently fixed by open PRs #13241 and #12533, both of whose full-Exec replacements conflict with this PR's new selection and lookup logic (merges/13241/result and merges/12533/result). When merging either fix, retain both full desktop argv parsing and explicit browser selection, rather than preserving the first-token line.
leads.triage: wrapped Exec pre-existing; #13241/#12533 OPEN verified via gh, Opus self-check confirmed merge-tree conflicts; published as related-PR note only

leads.summary: A global webapp app-ID mapping in another open PR may attach an ID to the wrong browser after changing this preference
leads.consequence: #12522 stores URL -> app ID in one map and its launcher resolves the binary from the regular browser. This PR allows switching the web-app browser independently, including to Helium. If the PRs are combined by simply keeping app-ID selection and using this preference for the binary, an app ID recorded in Chromium's profile can be sent to Helium's different profile. The other PR is diverged and merge-file detects an actual conflict (merges/12522/result:6-54); the exact runtime result of an unknown app ID in Helium is not verified. Reconcile by recording/looking up IDs per selected browser/profile or using --app= for a browser without a registered ID; test switching after promotion.
leads.triage: hypothesis about combined implementation with #12522; dropped

leads.summary: New webapp-browser menu choices have no test of checked/visibility guards
leads.consequence: The amended menu test checks only regular Browser labels. The new feature test parses the menu solely to inspect Helium's Remove action. A plausible typo such as changing the new Web App Browser/Helium checked comparison to `helium-browser.desktop` or dropping its when predicate leaves both tests green but gives users a missing selection check or an uninstallable choice in the menu. Assert all new selector labels, when predicates and checked IDs against command outputs under installed and absent browser cases.
leads.triage: menu checked/when untested; Opus verified guards by probe; not published as test note

leads.summary: Copy URL native messaging host registration omits Helium's real profile directory
leads.consequence: When Helium support is completed by enabling the bundled Chromium Copy URL extension, omarchy-install-chromium-copy-url writes com.omarchy.copy_url.json into the listed Chromium, Chrome, Brave and Edge profile roots but not into Helium's upstream-defined XDG_CONFIG_HOME/net.imput.helium/NativeMessagingHosts. Thus the Helium extension cannot reach the local Copy URL host even if the installer starts invoking the helper. Add `$HOME/.config/net.imput.helium` to browser_dirs, and account for XDG_CONFIG_HOME if respecting a relocated profile; cover it with a fixture. The older migration's ~/.config/helium is not the current upstream profile root.
leads.triage: contradicted: Opus follow-up (opus/followup-1-nmh.md) shows Helium 0.18.1.1 (imputnet/helium@b38c4bdd) applies scan-chrome-native-messaging-hosts.patch, falling back to ~/.config/google-chrome/NativeMessagingHosts which Omarchy populates; dropped, draft states no NMH change needed

leads.summary: Download Video native messaging host registration omits Helium's real profile directory
leads.consequence: The analogous com.omarchy.ytdlp.json installer enumerates Chromium/Chrome/Brave/Edge profile roots but omits the upstream-defined net.imput.helium profile. If Helium loads the Download Video extension after browser flags are integrated, its Alt+Shift+D host is still not registered. Add `$HOME/.config/net.imput.helium` to this list too (plus XDG_CONFIG_HOME where appropriate); assert the Helium manifest path in tests.

leads.summary: Helium webapp windows may miss the existing browser tiling/opacity rule
leads.consequence: The existing Hypr browser rule includes bare helium but not the reported `helium-<host>__<path>-<profile>` class form of --app windows. Open PR #9882 specifically adds a suffix and a test for the Helium webapp class, while this PR newly advertises Helium as the explicit webapp browser. Hypr's full-match semantics and Helium's runtime class should be checked at the shipped versions before claiming this verified; if confirmed, the chosen webapps retain default tiling/opacity rather than the browser rules. #9882 changes no file this PR touches so can merge separately.
leads.triage: hypothesis on Hypr window class; dropped

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Reviewed at `853d6bf`. **Verified:** the web-app browser preference behaves as described in the tested scope. Two gaps are worth addressing: Helium installs without the Chromium-family setup the other browsers get, and a missing web-app browser fails silently outside a terminal.

**Verified:** in Automatic mode, with the default `XDG_DATA_HOME` and whenever the browser's desktop entry exists, `omarchy-launch-webapp` passes the same `uwsm-app` arguments on this head as on the merge base (`2fbac0c`) and current `quattro` (`3faafba`). It differs only when no desktop entry exists (last row). The probe used a URL with a path, query and fragment plus an extra `--class=An app` argument. Every backend was a stub.

| Regular default | Merge base / `quattro` | This PR (Automatic) |
|---|---|---|
| `brave-browser.desktop` | brave | brave |
| `helium.desktop` | helium-browser | helium-browser |
| `chromium`, `firefox`, `zen` or empty | chromium | chromium |
| `vivaldi-stable.desktop`, no desktop entry | `uwsm-app -- --app=URL` (no browser) | exit 1 with a message |

**Verified:**
- An explicit selection is saved as a desktop ID under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omarchy/webapp-browser`. It applies regardless of the regular default. When that browser is removed, the launch exits 1 and nothing starts.
- `zen` and `firefox` are rejected, as is an uninstalled browser.
- `omarchy default webapp-browser` routes to the new command.
- The menu's `checked` strings match the IDs the command writes, and the `when` guards show only installed browsers.
- The package name, desktop ID and command used for Helium match the AUR `helium-browser-bin` package (`helium.desktop`, `Exec=helium-browser %U`).
- `webapp-browser-test.sh`, `default-apps-test.sh`, `menu-test.sh` and `menu-guards-test.sh` pass on the head and on a local merge into `quattro`. The new test fails on the merge base, and on mutants that ignore the preference or fall back to Chromium when the selected browser is missing.

### Helium is installed without the Chromium-family flags and theme setup

In `bin/omarchy-install-browser`, the new `helium)` case (lines 86-90) only installs the package and announces it. Every other Chromium-based case also runs `setup_chromium_policy_directory`, `copy_chromium_flags ~/.config/<browser>-flags.conf` and `omarchy-theme-set-browser`:

```text
chromium / chrome / edge / brave / brave-origin:
  pkg add -> policy directory -> copy_chromium_flags -> theme-set-browser -> announce
helium (this PR):
  pkg add -> announce
```

The AUR wrapper reads `~/.config/helium-browser-flags.conf`, which Omarchy never writes. Among the flags in `config/chromium-flags.conf`, Helium therefore misses:
- `--load-extension=` for Omarchy's bundled Copy URL, yt-dlp and WhatsApp Slim extensions.
- `--password-store=gnome-libsecret`, which `migrations/1784508556.sh` pins for the other Chromium-family browsers to prevent cookie and login loss on Hyprland.

In addition, `bin/omarchy-theme-set-browser` does not ask a running Helium to reload policy (`--refresh-platform-policy`) as it does for the other Chromium browsers, so a theme change reaches Helium only when its own policy watcher picks it up.

**Impact:** the PR adds Helium to Install > Browser and to Setup > Defaults > Browser (which installs on demand through this path). `manual/25-web-apps.md` uses Helium as its example web-app browser, and the same page promises `Shift + Alt + L` to copy the URL in a web app, which comes from the Copy URL extension. The native messaging hosts need no change: the Helium build that `helium-browser-bin` ships also reads `~/.config/google-chrome/NativeMessagingHosts`, which Omarchy already populates. Helium was not run; the missing extensions follow from source reading of the wrapper and flags.

**Suggested change:** under `helium)`, add `copy_chromium_flags ~/.config/helium-browser-flags.conf` and `omarchy-theme-set-browser`, plus `setup_chromium_policy_directory /etc/chromium/policies/managed` for parity. Remove that flags file in the Helium case of `omarchy-remove-browser`, and add a Helium line to `omarchy-theme-set-browser`. Open PRs #12132 and #5553 make similar Helium changes, so one of them may overlap with this part.

### A missing web-app browser fails without a visible message

Both failure branches in `bin/omarchy-launch-webapp` (lines 19 and 26) only write to stderr and exit 1. Web apps are normally started without a terminal: from `applications/*.desktop` entries, Hyprland bindings and menu actions. With the selected browser removed, a probe showed exit 1, the message on stderr only, and no `omarchy-notification-send` call.

**Impact:** after removing the selected web-app browser, clicking a web app does nothing visible. The PR description says the launcher "reports how to choose another browser", which holds only when it runs from a terminal. `omarchy-remove-browser` resets the regular default when it matches but never checks the web-app preference.

**Suggested change:** also call `omarchy-notification-send` with the same guidance on both branches (`bin/omarchy-launch-screensaver` does this). Optionally, have `omarchy-remove-browser` reset the preference to `auto`, or print a note, when it removes the selected web-app browser.

**Install on demand:** `omarchy default webapp-browser helium`, the example in `manual/25-web-apps.md`, fails with `Install helium before selecting it as the web app browser.` when Helium is missing. The line above it, `omarchy default browser zen`, installs on demand. Either add an `omarchy install browser helium` step to the manual or install on demand as `omarchy-default-browser` does.

**Optional test improvement:** the `uwsm-app` stub in `webapp-browser-test.sh` runs `exec "$@"`. In a sandboxed run where a regressed launcher (the merge-base version inside the head tree) resolved the system `chromium.desktop`, the test started the real Chromium binary. Replacing the stub's `exec "$@"` with `printf '%s\0' "$@" > "$TEST_LAUNCH"` (after the existing `--` check and `shift`) keeps a failing launcher from starting a browser on a developer machine.

**Small notes:**
- The summary line of `omarchy-launch-webapp` still says "in the default supported browser".
- The branch conflicts with current `quattro` only in `bin/omarchy-launch-webapp`, where `quattro` already made the same `env -u BROWSER` change. Taking the PR's version resolves it, and the tests above pass on that merge.
- Open PRs #11164 (Ecosia), #13241 and #12533 (full `Exec=` parsing) change the same launcher lines. Whichever merges second should keep both changes.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the head, the merge base and current `quattro`, plus the AUR `helium-browser-bin` package, the Helium 0.18.1.1 patch set and build configuration with the relevant Chromium 154 files, and the Zen and Firefox sources cited in the PR's `docs/zen-webapps-research.md`. The repository tests and behavioural probes of the launcher, the preference command, the dispatcher and the menu guards ran in a sandbox with the desktop and package backends stubbed, on the head, on a local merge into `quattro` and on base trees. Helium, Zen and a live desktop were not run, and the new submenu was not tested in the graphical menu.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
